newsitem.title: USA: US stocks stagger lower as profit-taking dominates.
newsitem.headline: US stocks stagger lower as profit-taking dominates.

text.p: Wall Street stocks succumbed to a wave of profit-taking on Wednesday, as the momentum from their most recent surge finally dissipated.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 35 points to close unofficially at 6727, snapping at its streak of record-high closes at four. Technology stocks were especially hard hit, reversing their powerful gains on Tuesday.
"Today was a mirror image of yesterday," said Tom Carpenter, managing director at ASB Capital Management Inc. "Let's face it, there have been phenomenal returns in stocks."
International Business Machines Corp slipped 2-3/4 to 164-1/4, the steepest loss among Dow components.

Perhaps more disappointing for investors, however, was a big decline in Intel Corp, which skidded 4-7/8 to 142-1/4, in the first trading since the company reported fourth-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street estimates.

While some of the drop reflected the same profit-taking impulse that afflicted the entire sector, some of the pressure came from concern that Intel's results had finally set a standard that even the chip maker itself could no longer surpass.
Interest rates proved another source of pressure for stocks, as the bond market also relinquished some of its most gains in the absence of any significant economic news.

Despite the decline in blue chips and technology stocks, the broad market was actually a fairly mixed picture, with breadth showing advancing and declining issues in a virtual dead heat on more than 500 million shares in total NYSE volume.
Medical device company St. Jude Medical Inc dropped 1-7/8 to 37 amid concerns that the company and others in the field may not meet fourth-quarter earnings expectations.
Tencor Instruments shot up 5-3/8 to 35-7/8 after news of its agreement to merge with semiconductor equipment maker KLA Instruments Corp, which shed 3/8 to 40-1/2.
Internet navigational service Yahoo Inc rose 4-1/2 to 25-3/8 after Hambrecht & Quist upgraded its rating on the stock to strong buy from buy.
Clarify Inc shares tumbled 11-1/2 to 34-1/2 after the software company's quarterly earnings disappointed some investors.
